sites.name: Colosseum
sites.fact: Opened in AD 80. It held around 50,000 spectators and is still the largest amphitheatre ever built.
sites.hint: The great oval ruin east of the Forum.

sites.name: St. Peter's Basilica
sites.fact: The dome, designed by Michelangelo, rises about 136 metres. The present church was completed in 1626.
sites.hint: The huge dome west of the Tiber, behind an oval square.

sites.name: Pantheon
sites.fact: Completed around AD 126. Its dome is still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world, open to the sky at the top.
sites.hint: A low grey dome in the old centre, east of Piazza Navona.

sites.name: Trevi Fountain
sites.fact: Finished in 1762. Tradition says a coin thrown over your shoulder means you will return to Rome.
sites.hint: In a small square in the old centre, east of the Pantheon.

sites.name: Roman Forum
sites.fact: The centre of public life in ancient Rome: markets, temples, courts and speeches, for about a thousand years.
sites.hint: The field of ruins between the Colosseum and the white Vittoriano.

sites.name: Circus Maximus
sites.fact: A chariot-racing track about 600 metres long that could hold some 150,000 people.
sites.hint: The long grassy hollow south of the Palatine Hill.

sites.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
sites.fact: Built as the tomb of the emperor Hadrian, finished in AD 139, and later used by the popes as a fortress.
sites.hint: The round fortress on the Tiber, east of St. Peter's.

sites.name: Piazza Navona
sites.fact: The long oval follows a stadium built by the emperor Domitian. Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers stands in the middle.
sites.hint: A long narrow square west of the Pantheon.

sites.name: Spanish Steps
sites.fact: 135 steps, built in the 1720s to link the square below with the church above.
sites.hint: Below a twin-towered church, north of the Trevi Fountain.

sites.name: Villa Borghese
sites.fact: A landscape park of about 80 hectares, laid out in the 1600s around the Borghese family's villa.
sites.hint: The big park north of the Spanish Steps.

sites.name: Vittoriano
sites.fact: A white marble monument to Victor Emmanuel II, the first king of united Italy, completed in 1935. Romans nicknamed it the typewriter.
sites.hint: The very white monument at the north end of the Forum.

sites.name: Stadio Olimpico
sites.fact: Rome's main stadium, home to both Roma and Lazio. It hosted the 1960 Olympic Games.
sites.hint: Beside a bend of the Tiber in the north of the city.
